meaning.evidence: C^k(K) consists of functions on compact K whose derivatives through order k are continuous; completeness in its usual norm and pointwise multiplication give the Banach-algebra structure used here.

notation.evidence: C^k(K) names the working algebra, while C^0 names the space in which the same iteration already has its limit.

prerequisites.evidence: The sentence supplies the compact interval, derivative order, continuity, completeness, and pointwise multiplication; the preceding argument supplies the iteration.

proof_job.evidence: This space gives (A.3), transfers the C^0 limit to higher derivatives, and controls each fixed derivative and compact parameter set.

target.exact_quote:
\NSi{NS-F-P128-001}{C^k(K)}, the space of functions on the compact interval whose derivatives through the stated order
are continuous. This space is complete in its usual norm, and pointwise multiplication makes it an algebra. That is the
Banach algebra used here, and the argument gives \eqref{eq:A.3}. The iterations are the same ones as
in \NSi{NS-F-P128-002}{C^0}, so they have the same limit. Every other fixed derivative
is finite by implicit differentiation, with a constant that may depend on the corresponding
data. Any extra parameter in a fixed compact set, such as the pulse amplitude below, is
handled in exactly the same way.
